correctness.rationale: The proof decomposes the state into the constant Neumann mode and the heat-evolving orthogonal complement. On a hypothetical finite-accumulation tail, intervals tend to zero and hence are shorter than one; the constant-mode amplitude is then bounded. A nonzero high-mode component remains nonzero at finite time and has bounded derivative away from t=0, giving a positive lower bound on the state norm and a linear increment bound that contradict the trigger at intervals tending to zero. The pure constant mode has a fixed positive interval, and the zero state has no events.
